name: Hercules
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Hercules, CA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Hercules, CA: the free city tree lighting with Santa and a toy drive at the Refugio Valley fire station.
lede: Hercules keeps its holiday season community sized: a free tree lighting with Santa at the Community Center and a firehouse toy drive on Refugio Valley Road.
celebrates: The City of Hercules marks the start of the holiday season with a free Holiday Tree Lighting in the Community Center parking lot at 2001 Refugio Valley Road. Families can have a photo taken with Santa, who lights the tree, and are invited to bring canned food, gently used coats or unwrapped toys to give. On the same road, Fire Station 76 hosts the Contra Costa County Fire Protection District's Santa's Firehouse Toy Drive, one of four firehouse stops Santa makes around the county.
lastyear: In 2025 the City of Hercules announced its annual tree lighting on its own Instagram page for Sunday, December 7, from 3:30 to 5:30 pm at the City Hall Civic Center, 111 Civic Drive, with Santa lighting the tree at about 5:15 pm. This year the city moved the afternoon to the Community Center parking lot on Refugio Valley Road.
facts: Hercules is named for the Hercules Powder Company, which took its name from its main product, a patented dynamite called Hercules powder, itself named after the Roman hero. The site began in 1881 as a manufacturing facility of the California Powder Works for dynamite, and the Hercules Powder Company took over in 1882. Explosives manufacturing was discontinued in 1964, and in 2000 the city began planning to turn its industrial waterfront into a walkable, mixed use town.
trains: Railroads came early to Hercules. The Central Pacific Railroad ran the first rail lines across the waterfront in late 1878, and the Atchison, Topeka and Santa Fe Railroad came through around 1899, on a right of way now used by BNSF. A Hercules stop on the Capitol Corridor line has been planned. For now, Amtrak's Capitol Corridor stops in nearby Martinez, and the San Francisco Bay Trail runs along the waterfront.
traditions: A free city event with photos with Santa and a Santa lit tree.
Families bring canned food, gently used coats or unwrapped toys to the tree lighting.
Santa visits Fire Station 76 to collect new, unwrapped toys for local children.
The toy drive includes a cookie and a chance to meet local firefighters.
kidfact: Hercules is named after a Roman hero and a dynamite factory, and its fire station is where Santa stops to collect toys.
faq: What is the main Christmas event in Hercules?

The City of Hercules' free Holiday Tree Lighting. It takes place in the Community Center parking lot at 2001 Refugio Valley Road, with photo opportunities with Santa, who lights the tree at about 5:15 pm, and a collection of food, coats and toys.
Is the Hercules tree lighting free?

Yes. The City of Hercules' calendar lists the event as free. Families are invited to bring canned food items, gently used coats or unwrapped toys as part of the afternoon. Santa is there for photo opportunities and will light the tree at about 5:15 pm, near the end of the event.
Can kids meet Santa at a fire station in Hercules?

Yes. Santa's Firehouse Toy Drive at Fire Station 76, 1680 Refugio Valley Road, is one of four stops Santa makes across the county. Families donate a new, unwrapped toy, have a cookie and meet their local firefighters, according to the Contra Costa County Fire Protection District's calendar.
Why is the city called Hercules?

It was named for the Hercules Powder Company, which took its name from a patented dynamite called Hercules powder, itself named after the Roman hero. The site began making dynamite in 1881, and explosives manufacturing there was discontinued in 1964.
Is there a train in Hercules?

Not for passengers yet. A Hercules stop on the Capitol Corridor line has been planned, but for now the nearest Amtrak Capitol Corridor station is in Martinez. The San Francisco Bay Trail runs along the Hercules waterfront for families who like to walk or bike.
sources: Contra Costa County Fire Protection District
